**Sparkassen add subscriptions, one-click and buyer protection to Wero**

*Germany's largest banking group is rolling out the checkout features Wero needs to compete with card networks, but fragmented adoption across individual savings banks could limit the impact.*

Subscription payments, one-click checkout and optional buyer protection are now available or imminent for Sparkassen customers using Wero, following an announcement on Monday (November 24) by S-Payment, the payments subsidiary of the German savings banks group. Subscription billing has been technically possible since late September, but S-Payment's announcement confirmed the capability for Sparkassen customers, with one-click checkout due by the end of November. An optional online buyer protection programme has been live since early November, supplementing Wero's standard complaints process with insurance-backed cover for non-delivery and returns. Each Sparkasse decides independently whether to offer the buyer protection, creating uneven coverage across the network.

The features address a clear gap. Wero's e-commerce proposition in Germany has lacked the subscription billing, stored-credential checkout and consumer guarantees that card networks offer as standard. Without them, merchants had little reason to prefer Wero over Visa or Mastercard at checkout. One-click payments, which store a customer's details after the first purchase and remove the need for repeated strong customer authentication, are particularly important for conversion rates.

Sparkassen account for more than seven million of Wero's 11 million German registrations, according to figures from late October. The savings banks also plan to give customers access to the standalone Wero app from the European Payments Initiative (EPI), alongside the existing integration in the Sparkasse banking app. Wero's broader momentum is building: Valve added Wero as a payment method on Steam in Germany this week, and neobank bunq extended Wero to customers across all 27 EU member states on November 20. The question is whether feature parity at the Sparkassen translates into merchant adoption quickly enough to give Wero commercial traction before the novelty of its European sovereignty pitch wears thin.

**FCA to open targeted engagement on UK open finance framework early next year**

*Roundtables and bilateral meetings will draw on findings from the Smart Data Accelerator, the Prism Taskforce and the Mills AI review as the regulator moves from roadmap to practical policy design.*

Targeted stakeholder engagement on open finance will begin at the start of 2027, Andrew Self, head of open banking and open finance at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), told delegates at Open Banking Expo UK and Europe 2026 in London on Sunday (November 24). The engagement will not present a settled regulatory model but will instead explore the choices facing policymakers and invite further evidence from industry.

The announcement comes as the government prepares to consult in 2027 on how to deliver the benefits of open finance, initially focusing on SME lending. Self said the forthcoming engagement would bring together findings from the FCA's Smart Data Accelerator, its broader industry engagement, the Prism Taskforce and the Mills AI review examining AI's impact on financial services. He pointed to progress already made in open banking, including the June launch of the UK Payments Initiative and commercial variable recurring payments (VRP), and industry-led work to establish a future open banking entity.

Self framed trust as the central constraint on scaling open finance. "Trust is what allows it to scale," he told delegates, while acknowledging that further work is needed to establish a sustainable long-term regulatory framework for open banking alongside the development of open finance. "This isn't an invitation for firms to wait until every part of open finance is settled," he added. "It's an invitation to engage now and help shape the future of open finance."

**Fabrick builds shared platform to ready Italian banks for digital euro**

*A shared-infrastructure platform designed to reduce the integration burden on banks preparing for a potential digital euro launch has been developed by the Italian open finance firm.*

Fabrick, an Italian open finance infrastructure provider, has unveiled a platform called Digital Euro Rail One, designed as shared infrastructure to help banks prepare for the operational demands of a digital euro. The platform is intended to reduce the cost and complexity of integrating with the ECB's planned digital euro architecture by offering a common technical layer that multiple banks can use rather than each building bespoke connections.

The timing aligns with the ECB's selection of 36 payment providers for its digital euro pilot phase and the European Parliament's vote in July to advance the digital euro regulation to final negotiations. With trilogue discussions ongoing and merchant fee structures still contested, banks face the practical challenge of preparing for a system whose final design remains uncertain. Fabrick's approach, offering a multi-tenant platform rather than a bespoke integration for each institution, reflects a bet that shared infrastructure will be more efficient than individual bank builds.

Italy has been among the more active euro area markets in digital euro preparation, with CBI, Bancomat and Nexi signing a memorandum of understanding on November 20 for their own joint infrastructure effort. The parallel initiative from Fabrick suggests the Italian market is treating digital euro readiness as a competitive space in its own right, not merely a compliance exercise.

**Form3 adds stablecoin payments to its infrastructure via Coinbase partnership**

*The integration connects crypto settlement to existing instant payments rails across the UK and Europe, extending a cloud-native platform already used by banks and financial institutions.*

Form3, a cloud-native payment infrastructure provider, is partnering with Coinbase to add stablecoin payment capabilities to its platform. The integration extends Form3's existing connectivity to instant payment rails in the UK, Europe and North America, enabling customers to move money using stablecoins alongside traditional fiat settlement.

Other payment infrastructure firms are making similar moves. Mastercard has added stablecoin settlement to its merchant network, Visa is backing the Open USD stablecoin and Bottomline has integrated stablecoin payments into corporate treasury. Stablecoin settlement is becoming a feature of mainstream payment infrastructure rather than a standalone product.

Form3's client base of banks and financial institutions faces a strategic question about whether stablecoin rails can offer meaningful advantages in speed or cost for specific use cases such as cross-border payouts. The Coinbase partnership positions Form3 to serve clients exploring that question without requiring them to build separate crypto infrastructure.
